introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Food and Nutrition 2 (0540), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2024. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Instructions to candidates: ANSWER ANY FOUR QUESTIONS.

You are reminded of the necessity of good English and orderly presentation of work. Tabulate wherever possible and use diagrams where appropriate.

Sujet scanné (CamScanner) de 2 pages : page de garde et six questions sur une page ; lu en image, aucun schéma ni figure imprimé, donc `figures` vide dans tous les fichiers. Filigranes (gcerevision.com, Kawlo) ignorés. L'en-tête imprimé « Food &Nutrition 2 » est recopié en « Food and Nutrition 2 » dans l'introduction ; les petites fautes de frappe du sujet (« five(5) », « Bring out five (5) importance of  food and nutrition », « types of food service  . ») sont recopiées telles quelles.

Points : chaque question imprime « Total = (25 marks) » et les points imprimés des sous-questions totalisent bien 25 pour les six questions (Q1 : 3+5+6+6+5 ; Q2 : 4+6+10+5 ; Q3 : 10+5+5+5 ; Q4 : 4+6+2+3+5+5 ; Q5 : 2+7+4+6+6 ; Q6 : 5+5+5+5+5) : aucun écart. Les sous-parties (i), (ii) restent dans le texte de la sous-question (d), 4(c), 4(d), 5(a) ou 6(d), dont `points` est la somme imprimée.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées, au nombre exact d'éléments demandé, avec quelques réponses acceptables supplémentaires entre parenthèses. Aucune composition chiffrée de plat ou d'aliment n'est avancée ; les seuls chiffres sont les valeurs énergétiques classiques de la question 3(b), recalculées avec Python.

Question 1(d)(i) : les règles de friture sont les règles usuelles d'un cours (huile remplie à moitié au plus, huile chauffée avant d'ajouter l'aliment, aliment séché, petites quantités, égouttage). Aucune température précise n'est donnée, le test du morceau de pain est utilisé à la place. Question 1(c) : l'explication de la couleur de la viande reste volontairement générale (pas de nom de pigment).

questions.enonce_markdown:
List three (3) types of kitchens

(3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Three types of kitchens (1 mark each):

1. **Traditional (rural) kitchen** - a separate hut or shed behind the house, with an open fire or a three-stone hearth.
2. **Modern (fitted) kitchen** - a room inside the house with a cooker (gas or electric), a sink, work surfaces, cupboards and often a refrigerator.
3. **Institutional (commercial) kitchen** - a large kitchen that cooks for many people, for example in a hotel, a restaurant, a school canteen or a hospital.

(Other acceptable answers: kitchenette, a small kitchen in a flat or student room; kitchen-diner or open-plan kitchen, where the cooking and eating areas are together.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Mention five (5) factors that can influence the size of a family kitchen

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Five factors that can influence the size of a family kitchen (1 mark each):

1. **The number of people in the family.** A large family needs a bigger kitchen, with more working and storage space, than a small family.
2. **The money available (the budget).** A bigger kitchen costs more to build, to furnish and to equip.
3. **The space available in the house or on the plot.** The kitchen cannot be larger than the land or the plan of the house allows.
4. **The amount and type of cooking done.** A family that cooks large meals, entertains guests often or prepares food for sale needs more space and equipment.
5. **The equipment and storage needed.** A kitchen with a cooker, a refrigerator, a freezer, a table and many cupboards must be larger than one with a single stove.

(Other acceptable answers: whether the family also eats in the kitchen; the number of people who work in the kitchen at the same time; the needs of an elderly or disabled person; the climate and the way of life of the family.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
State six (6) effects of heat during the cooking of meat

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Six effects of heat on meat during cooking (1 mark each):

1. **The proteins coagulate (set).** The soft, raw protein of the muscle becomes firm, and the meat changes from soft and sticky to firm.
2. **The meat shrinks.** The muscle fibres contract and squeeze out water and juices, so the piece of meat becomes smaller and may become dry and hard if it is overcooked.
3. **The colour changes.** The red or pink colour of raw meat changes to brown or grey because the colouring matter of the meat is altered by the heat.
4. **The connective tissue softens.** Slow, moist cooking (stewing, boiling, braising) changes the tough collagen of the connective tissue into soft gelatine, so tough cuts become tender.
5. **The fat melts.** The fat in and around the meat becomes liquid and runs out, and it can be drained off.
6. **The flavour develops and the surface browns.** Cooking releases the juices and flavouring substances, giving the cooked meat its smell and taste, and dry heat browns the outside of the meat.

(Other correct points: the bacteria on the meat are destroyed, so the meat is safe to eat; some water-soluble vitamins and minerals are lost in the juices.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Outline six(6) rules of deep frying.

(6 marks)

(ii) Enumerate five (5) mechanical methods in raising mixtures.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Six rules of deep frying (1 mark each)**

1. **Use a deep, strong pan or deep fryer and do not fill it more than about half full of oil**, so that the oil cannot bubble over when the food is added.
2. **Use a good frying oil or fat and keep it clean.** Strain it after use to remove food particles, and do not use it again and again when it is dark or smells burnt.
3. **Heat the oil to the right temperature before adding the food.** A small piece of bread dropped into the hot oil should sizzle and turn golden quickly. If the oil is too cool the food absorbs fat and is greasy; if it is too hot the outside burns while the inside stays raw.
4. **Dry the food well, or coat it** (with batter, flour, or egg and breadcrumbs) before frying, because wet food makes the hot oil spit.
5. **Fry a small quantity at a time.** Too much food at once lowers the temperature of the oil and makes the food greasy.
6. **Lower the food gently into the oil and lift it out with a basket or a slotted spoon, then drain it on absorbent paper.** Never leave the hot pan alone, and never pour water on burning oil (cover it with a lid or a damp cloth).

**(ii) Five mechanical methods of raising mixtures (1 mark each)**

Mechanical methods raise a mixture by trapping **air** in it; the air expands in the heat of the oven and makes the mixture rise.

1. **Sieving** the flour (and other dry ingredients) to add air.
2. **Creaming** the fat and sugar together until light and fluffy.
3. **Whisking** eggs, or eggs and sugar, to a foam.
4. **Beating** a batter or a mixture with a spoon, fork or whisk.
5. **Rubbing in** the fat to the flour with the fingertips, lifting the mixture to trap air.

(Other correct answers: folding in the flour gently so as not to lose the air; rolling and folding the dough in layers, as in flaky and puff pastry.)
